In biology , offspring ( / ˈ ɒ f s p r ɪ ŋ / ) are the young creation of living organisms , produced either by sexual or asexual reproduction . Collective offspring may be known as a brood or progeny . This can refer to a set of simultaneous offspring, such as the chicks hatched from one clutch of eggs , or to all offspring produced over time, as with the honeybee .  Offspring can occur after mating , artificial insemination , or as a result of cloning .
